slides.title: Amoxicillin
slides.highlight: Rash (esp. in EBV) & diarrhea; adjust in renal failure; avoid chewables in PKU.
slides.moa: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins, causing cell lysis.
doses: Neonate to ≤3 mo: 20–30 mg/kg/day PO ÷ 12 hrly
Child ≥3 mo (standard): 25–50 mg/kg/day PO ÷ 8–12 hrly; max 2–3 g/day (up to 4 g/day)
Child ≥3 mo (high dose, AOM/CAP): 80–90 mg/kg/day PO ÷ 8–12 hrly; max 2–3 g/day (up to 4 g/day)
Strep pharyngitis (child): 50 mg/kg/day PO ÷ 12 hrly × 10 days; max 1 g/day

caption:
Why do we double the amoxicillin dose in paediatric pneumonia and acute otitis media? 💊

In OPDs and NEET-PG exams, knowing standard vs high-dose amoxicillin is essential. High-dose therapy (80–90 mg/kg/day) with 8-hourly dosing maximises time above MIC to overcome penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae. Remember: it achieves roughly double the serum levels of oral ampicillin with fewer GI side effects, and requires renal dose adjustment!
